text:
sasha: quick follow-up from the RFC: we need a concrete operator <-> control-plane contract for headroom reservations and lifecycle events. the current ambiguity is causing unexpected admission behavior in staging.

ben: agree. can we list required RPCs + events first? my proposal: RPCs: `ReserveHeadroom(tenant, slots, ttl_ms, idempotency_token) -> reservation_id, eta_ms`, `ReleaseReservation(reservation_id)`, `AbortReservation(reservation_id)`. Events: `POOL_READY`, `POOL_DRAINING`, `POOL_SCALE_COMPLETE`, `RESERVATION_EXPIRED`, `RESERVATION_ABORTED`.

maria: +1. add a `ReservationStatus` stream so control-plane can subscribe instead of polling. include fields: state, slots_allocated, slots_failed, eta_ms, last_update_ts.

oliver: streaming is fine but beware of ordering guarantees. we should mandate each event include a monotonically increasing sequence and the reservation_id. retries must be deduped by idempotency token.

kevin: operational concern: operator knows GPU types and warmup quirks. it should return a `warmup_profile` for the model+hw combo when ReserveHeadroom is called so control-plane can compute realistic ETA. profile: `cold_p50_ms`, `cold_p95_ms`, `kv_restore_ms`, `gpu_type`.

ben: good call. add `failed_warmup_reason` to the scale result. operator should emit final `PoolScaleResult` with counters {ready, warming, failed}. that makes billing reconciliation trivial.

sasha: about billing: control-plane keeps accounting but needs authoritative signals from operator. RPCs must include `accepts_charges: bool` in the reservation ack so we don't bill when operator declines.

maria: telemetry gap: right now prometheus only scrapes node counts. we need slot-level metrics. propose names: `redwood_pool_slots_total{pool}`, `redwood_pool_slots_ready{pool}`, `redwood_pool_slots_warming{pool}`, `redwood_pool_slots_failed{pool}`, `redwood_pool_warmup_p95_ms{pool,model}`. will open a PR.

oliver: also add an event sink for lifecycle logs: `pool_event_log{pool}` with structured entries. helps postmortems.

kevin: drain behavior needs standardization. default: graceful drain window = 30s, notify control-plane with `drain_started(pool, eviction_deadline_ts)` then `drain_progress(pool, inflight_requests)` and finally `drain_complete(pool)`. operator must provide a config knob for `force_after_ms` where it will forcibly terminate.

ben: edgecase: double reservation races. if operator can only honor one reservation, it needs deterministic tie-breaker. control-plane should send sorted reservation priority list in a single RPC `SubmitReservations(list)` when contention detected. operator will return accepted subset and rejected list with reason codes.

sasha: fallback routing: control-plane should not block forever. add per-tenant `max_wait_ms` and an admission decision: route->fallback_model or queue. document default fallback to `model.small-quant` variant.

maria: please also require webhooks to be signed HMAC-SHA256 with key id headers. polling fallback still allowed for customers behind proxies.

oliver: for testing, we need a harness that simulates: slow warmup, partial failures, rapid cancel/replace of reservations. qa-bot: can you author a test matrix?

qa-bot: will do. suggest matrix dims: warmup latency (fast/slow), reservation collision (none/2x/3x), drain mode (grace/force), network flakiness (none/sporadic). will output pass/fail criteria.

kevin: infra cost note: adding signed webhooks + sequence logs requires ~2x storage for event backlog for 7 days. estimate added S3 + lambda processing cost ~ $1.2k/month for staging footprint; will refine.

ben: another API nit: include `eta_uncertainty_ms` so control-plane can SLO-budget conservatively. operator can set this from warmup_profile variance.

sasha: good. also require operator publish `last_scale_duration_ms` and `last_failed_warmups` gauge. add label `gpu_family` for heterogenous pools.

maria: implementing slot-level metrics will require a small change in operator exporters; I'll include migration notes so older metric names keep returning node counts until FF enabled.

oliver: failure modes doc: I'll draw sequence diagrams: happy path, reservation timeout, partial fail, operator crash during warmup. I'll include recovery steps and control-plane fallback policies.

ben: let's also decide on a backpressure signal from control-plane to operator: `admission_rate_limit(tenant, max_rps)` RPC so operator can throttle inbound routing to preserve SLO when under stress.

kevin: tricky: operator isn't in the fast path of routing decisions for hosted users. but for dedicated pools we can wire that signal. ok from infra side.

sasha: action items: ben -> draft RPC + event contract with example payloads and idempotency semantics (due Fri). maria -> prometheus metric PR + migration plan (due Tue). oliver -> diagrams + failure modes (due Tue). kevin -> infra cost + webhook feasibility (due Mon). qa-bot -> test matrix and canary harness proposal (due Wed).

maria: small request: add `reserve_headroom` response include `allocated_gpu_types` array so control-plane can match runtime perf.

ben: done. will include it. also will add sample protobufs and curl examples in the draft.

deploy-bot: note: feature-flag rollout scheduled `operator-api-v2` -> canary staging 06:00UTC tomorrow.

kevin: we'll need quota bump for canary; pinged infra ticket.

sasha: thanks all. we'll reconvene next week to sign off on the contract and the canary results.
